title: The While Loop
description: A loop that keeps going as long as a condition stays True.

content.real: Chewing while there is food in your mouth
content.text: You don't decide how many bites before you start. You just keep chewing **while** there is still food, however many bites that takes.

items.title: for loop
items.text: Repeats a set number of times, decided before it starts.

items.title: while loop
items.text: Repeats for as long as its condition stays `True`. You may not know the count in advance.

items: The **condition** of a `while` loop is a comparison, like `energy > 0`.
It is exactly the kind of comparison you wrote back in Module 2.
While it is `True`, the loop keeps going.

content.question: When does a while loop stop?
options: When it reaches the end of range()
content.explain: A `while` loop keeps going as long as its condition is `True`. The first time the check comes back `False`, the loop ends.

steps.label: Run

content.title: The three beats of every turn

content.value: Step through the tracer below to watch one full run.

content.after: Out of energy, time to rest!

content.code:
energy = 3
while energy > 0:
    print("Jumping jack!")
    energy = energy - 1
print("Out of energy, time to rest!")

steps.note: Update: `energy` goes down by 1. This is what moves the loop toward the end.
Check: `0 > 0` is `False`. The loop ends and Python skips past it.
This line is not indented, so it runs once, after the loop.
out: Out of energy, time to rest!

content.title: Check, run, update, by hand
content.outro: Three `True` checks gave three turns. The fourth check was `False`.

content.question: How many times does this print Go?
content.explain: `n` starts at 4. Each turn takes 2 away: 4, then 2, then 0. `0 > 0` is `False`, so there are 2 turns.

items: The condition only changes because something **inside** the loop changes it.
Take out the line that lowers `energy` and it stays at 3 forever.
The check is `True` every single time, so the loop never ends.
content.title: A loop that never stops

items.title: Stops
items.text: `energy` goes 3, 2, 1, 0. The check turns `False` and the loop ends.

items.title: Never stops
items.text: Nothing changes `energy`. It is 3 forever, so `energy > 0` is always `True`.

content.value: Switch off the update line in the tracer on the previous tab to see it happen.
Before you run a while loop, find the line that moves the condition toward `False`. If you cannot point at one, the loop will not stop.

content.question: Why does this loop never end?
options: `<` cannot be used in a while loop
content.explain: Nothing inside the loop changes `x`. It stays `0`, `0 < 5` is always `True`, and the loop runs forever.

items: A while loop can count, just like a for loop.
But you do the bookkeeping yourself.
Already know how many repeats you need? A `for` loop is usually simpler.

content.code:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print("Count is:", count)
    count += 1

steps.note: You create the counter yourself, before the loop.
You change the counter yourself too. `+= 1` adds one.

content.title: Watch the counter
content.outro: The loop counted 1 to 3, and `count` ended at 4.

content.value:
count = 1
while count <= 5:
    print("Count is:", count)
    count += 1
`count += 1` is a shortcut for `count = count + 1`. There is a matching `-=` for subtracting, like `energy -= 1`.
content.title: Shortcut

content.question: How many lines does this print?
content.explain: `count` goes 1, 2, 3. When it becomes 4, `count <= 3` is False and the loop ends.

quiz.question: When does a while loop stop?
options: When the computer is shut down.
quiz.explain: A while loop keeps going as long as its condition is True, and stops the moment a check comes back False.

quiz.question: What happens if a while loop's condition is always True?
quiz.explain: If nothing inside the loop moves the condition toward False, the loop never ends. That is an infinite loop.

quiz.question: How many times does this loop print?  n = 3  /  while n > 0:  print(n)  /  n -= 1
quiz.explain: n is 3, 2, then 1 on the three passes that print. On the fourth check n is 0, which is not greater than 0, so the loop ends.
